evidence.quote: The proposed methodology is conceptual and governance-oriented rather than empirical; therefore, it does not rely on a single predefined dataset.
To contextualize the proposed approach, its characteristics were compared with commonly used productivity evaluation methods, including output-centric metrics, DevOps-oriented
Rather than aggregating activity into a single metric, the methodology maps data sources to distinct productivity dimensions based on the SPACE framework proposed by Forsgren et al [1].

As illustrated in Fig. 2, the AI-assisted workflow produces paired outputs for each productivity dimension. Each output includes a normalized quantitative indicator and a corresponding natural-language explanation.

This paper framed AI-assisted productivity evaluation as a governance challenge rather than a technical optimization problem, emphasizing accountability, transparency, and ethical oversight in hybrid and remote work environments.
